environment.origin: Actual Livara GTK4 apps on Ubuntu 24.04 under Xvfb/Openbox; this is not a booted Livara desktop.

native_checks: Real Settings headerbar shows custom traffic lights
Stock title buttons are hidden while custom CSD is active
Native close button has an accessible semantic label
Settings diameter scale persisted its value
Live CSS enlarged actual native button allocation
Settings hex-color control persisted its value
Settings symbol switch updated the live controls
Right-side preference physically moved the native controls
Physical left-side preference survives an RTL headerbar
Traffic-light red/yellow/green order remains LTR under RTL
Native-style preference hides custom buttons
Native-style preference restores original stock-button visibility
Green native button entered real window-manager fullscreen
Green tooltip follows native fullscreen state
Actual F11 key left fullscreen through the GTK shortcut controller
Green maximize preference invokes real native maximize
Green maximize preference restores the native window
Actual Shift-click green maximizes instead of fullscreen
Yellow native button minimizes through the window manager
The minimized native window can be restored
Settings reduced-motion switch updates the desktop animation preference
Native Settings transitions stop under reduced motion
Custom red control respects an application's close-request guard
Destroying the controlled child releases settings and shortcut bindings
Generated and live GTK CSS produced zero parsing errors
Main native close action destroys the window and releases its binding

preloaded_managed_css_probe.origin: Actual Livara GTK4 apps on Ubuntu 24.04 under Xvfb/Openbox; this is not a booted Livara desktop.
preloaded_managed_css_probe.probe: Preloaded managed GTK4 user CSS then native/default style

known_limitations: Changing from traffic lights to native/default restores control visibility and actions immediately, but GTK user CSS loaded at process startup can remain active until that application is reopened.
These tests exercise GTK native windows and X11 Openbox window-manager state. They do not qualify GNOME Shell opening/closing effects, Wayland, login, installation or a booted Livara image.
Gallery resource availability and live system metrics describe the small Ubuntu 24.04 test container, not the complete target OS package set.
